author: BBC News
description:
Explicit images of the French activist Gisèle Pelicot have been sent to the media to promote a book about coercive control.
 
The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay.
 
Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious.
 
The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".
 
Pelicot said: "Today I find myself once again humiliated, exposed and hurt, as if the ordeal of the trial had not been enough.”

title: 'I cried for hours after losing UK university place'

author: BBC News
description:
Afghan students say they've been left devastated after the UK stopped accepting new study visa applications from Afghanistan.

Many had secured university places and scholarships after years of studying under Taliban restrictions, only to see those opportunities disappear. 

The UK says the measure is a temporary response to concerns over visa abuse and rising asylum claims.

title: Nvidia employees cheer and applaud as Jensen Huang returns to office as CEO. #Nvidia #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
Asian markets are surging, with chipmakers leading gains across the region, after Nvidia reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive - reuniting enthusiasm for AI trade.
 
South Korea's Kospi index is up by more than 6.8% while Japan's Nikkei 225 has jumped by 3.8%, as of around noon in East Asia.
 
Both benchmarks are deeply linked to the tech industry and have been driven by jumps in the shares of big names like SK Hynix, which is up by 8.5%.
 
US President Donald Trump said he "made the deal" for Huang's reinstatement, adding he had spoken to Nvidia's board both "directly and indirectly" about the co-founder.

title: Jensen Huang's return sends Nvidia and Asian stocks soaring | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
 
The company had come under pressure from US President Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to reverse course and bring Huang back.
 
Since returning last year to the White House, Trump has amassed a significant level of investment in Nvidia. Recent financial disclosures show he purchased $265,000 in its stock and sold as much as $15,000 worth of shares in September.
 
A BBC review of his government financial disclosures for the last two years shows he purchased shares of Nvidia stock worth between $23m and $86m (£18m and £66m). And he has bought Nvidia stock 85 separate times through a number of investment accounts.
